claims.text: A directed response is a new text written from a source for a form, audience and purpose the task sets, re-using the source’s content in a new style: it is not a summary of the source and not a copy of its wording.

claims.text: Reshaping a source runs in two steps: first select the content the new purpose needs, then change the register, voice and structure so the content arrives as the new form, in your own words.

claims.text: Re-using content means keeping what the source says — its facts, its viewpoint, its people — while putting it into your own words; lifting phrases or sentences from the source is copying, not re-use.

claims.text: Adding material the source does not support drifts the response into a different story, so every fact in a directed response traces back to the source.
